relationships.subject: capsaicin
relationships.evidence_quote: We reasoned that in co-cultures with DRG neurons, application of the potent TRPV1 agonist capsaicin (10 μM) would stimulate nociceptors to release Substance P and thereby activate neighboring Substance P-sniffer cells.

relationships.subject: Calca
relationships.evidence_quote: Thus, Calca deletion largely abolished endogenous CGRPα signaling.

relationships.subject: PGE2
relationships.evidence_quote: PGE2 injection elicited short-lasting heat and mechanical hypersensitivity to a similar extent in both WT and DKO mice (Figure 3C–D).

relationships.subject: Substance P
relationships.evidence_quote: Therefore, Substance P and CGRPα are dispensable for some forms of neurogenic inflammation.

relationships.subject: CGRPα
relationships.evidence_quote: Substance P and CGRPα are therefore not essential for mechanical or cold allodynia.

key_findings: Tac1/Calca double knockout mice lacking Substance P and CGRPα show intact acute, inflammatory, neuropathic pain and itch behaviors.
Capsaicin-evoked release of both peptides from DRG neurons is abolished in DKO, yet neurogenic inflammation and PGE2 sensitization persist.
